claim_text: An outside party got into Fugaku's operational network
summary: RIKEN says an external third party gained unauthorized access to the internal operational network of the Fugaku supercomputer between Nov 10 and Nov 13, 2026.
detail: RIKEN says it confirmed the access at 4:33 PM on Nov 13 (Japan time). Its first notice also gives Nov 12 as the day of the access; the window is Nov 10 to 13.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: RIKEN's own notices say so; the Japan Times reports it.

claim_text: The way in was the public operating-status dashboard
summary: RIKEN says the intruder used a publicly reachable web page that displays Fugaku's operating status (the dashboard) to get into the internal network.
detail: RIKEN says the exact method is still being investigated. Its first notice says it will fix vulnerabilities in the software that was exploited before restarting, but it has not named the software or the flaw. The page has been taken down, according to the Japan Times.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: RIKEN's first notice names the dashboard as the entry point.

claim_text: A missing security protection let them in
summary: TechRadar's headline says the facility 'was apparently lacking in some essential security protection', and The Register's headline calls Fugaku's security 'decidedly un-super'. Neither article says which protection was missing.
detail: RIKEN has not said so. RIKEN's second notice plans to separate public services from the administrative network.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Only headlines suggest it; neither RIKEN nor the articles' text names a specific missing control. TechRadar's report is based on The Register's, so they count as one source.

claim_text: Malicious programs were installed on some servers
summary: RIKEN says multiple internal servers were tampered with, and that some of the compromised servers had malicious programs installed.
detail: RIKEN says it is still investigating the details.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: RIKEN's first notice says so; the Japan Times repeats it.

claim_text: 430 stolen private keys for outside systems, 233 with no passphrase
summary: RIKEN says it has confirmed that authentication credentials such as SSH private keys, used to connect to systems outside RIKEN, were collected and taken from some users' home directories. It counts 430: 233 without a passphrase, 197 with.
detail: A private key without a passphrase can be used by whoever holds it. RIKEN is asking users to revoke and replace their keys.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: RIKEN's second notice gives the count and the breakdown.

claim_text: Up to 4,222 Fugaku users and 375 RIKYU users
summary: RIKEN says up to 4,222 Fugaku users and 375 RIKYU users may be affected. Its second notice says log analysis found traces that an intruder reached the targeted information for the 4,222 Fugaku users.
detail: RIKEN's first notice gives 4,222 in its overview but 4,224 in one list. The 375 RIKYU figure appears only in the first notice.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Both RIKEN notices give the counts; the Japan Times repeats them.

claim_text: Names, emails, user IDs, and registration details
summary: RIKEN says user names, emails and user IDs were or may have been taken. Its second notice adds registration details such as address, affiliation and phone number, and which type of document was used for identity checks.
detail: RIKEN says the identity documents themselves were not found to be leaked.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: RIKEN lists the data in both notices.

summary: RIKEN's first notice says there was, at that time, no evidence that research data or files were taken.
detail: Whether files holding other people's personal information were taken was still under investigation.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: RIKEN said this on Nov 16; TechRadar repeats that no evidence was found. We have not seen a later update.
notes: Japan's education and science minister repeated on Nov 17 that RIKEN had found no evidence research results were taken (s005).

claim_text: The intruder tried the stolen keys on other systems
summary: RIKEN says it confirmed that the intruder tried to connect to other systems using some of the credentials, and its second notice says it has evidence of external connections for some credentials.
detail: RIKEN says it has found no other misuse.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: RIKEN says so in both notices.

claim_text: Break-ins at other organizations using the stolen keys
summary: RIKEN has found no other misuse of the credentials. The Register (and TechRadar, citing it) says RIKEN is working with other supercomputer operators to check whether the attacker got in; no intrusion there is confirmed.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: RIKEN says it found no other instances of misuse so far.

claim_text: Fugaku has been offline since Nov 14, with no restart date
summary: RIKEN says it suspended Fugaku at 4:30 AM on Nov 14 (Japan time) and blocked outside access. Restart will follow measures such as separating public services from the administrative network and rebuilding servers.
detail: TechRadar says Fugaku went offline after someone tried to use compromised credentials on Nov 13. RIKEN's notices give Nov 14 as the shutdown time.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: RIKEN gives the time and the conditions for restart.

claim_text: Police and government agencies have been told
summary: RIKEN says it explained the incident to the Saitama Prefectural Police on Nov 16 and the Hyogo Prefectural Police on Nov 16 and 19, and is sending further reports to government agencies.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: RIKEN's second notice gives the dates.

summary: No person or group has been named, and we found no claim of responsibility.
detail: RIKEN says 'intruder(s)' and 'an external third party'.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: None of the sources names an attacker.

claim_text: Keys that give administrator access to Fugaku's servers were taken
summary: Japan's education and science minister said RIKEN reported on Nov 14 that keys allowing administrator-level access to servers that make up Fugaku had been taken out, and that RIKEN then cut outside access and replaced the keys.
detail: RIKEN's first notice says it replaced the administrative keys at 8:20 PM on Nov 14 (Japan time).
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The minister's own press conference transcript says so; RIKEN's notice records the key replacement.

claim_text: RIKEN is setting up an investigative committee with outside experts
summary: RIKEN says it will set up an investigative committee that includes outside experts and will compile a reform plan.
detail: Japan's education and science minister also announced the committee on Nov 20, according to Kyodo and Nikkei.
label: Confirmed

claim_text: Other supercomputer operators were asked to check their systems
summary: Japan's education ministry shared what is known about the intrusion route with universities and research institutes that run supercomputers and asked them to check their systems and take countermeasures.
detail: On Nov 17 the minister said the ministry would move quickly to strengthen security across Japan's shared research computing network (HPCI).
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Nikkei and Kyodo report the request independently; the minister's Nov 17 transcript covers the wider security push. The Nov 20 transcript was not yet posted.
